jobs.title: Program Coordinator
jobs.description:
Organization Description: 

Colorado Food Cluster (CFC) Inc. partners with community organizations throughout Colorado to provide critical support, resources and services to students and their families. Through culturally responsive approaches, CFC provides nutritious meals to children and families throughout Colorado leveraging federally funded programs. CFC continuously seeks opportunities and programs that remove barriers to access food, for all people in our communities using innovative solutions to improve access to nutritious food.

Job Overview:

The Program Coordinator will support the successful implementation of the Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) and Summer Food Service Program (SFSP), ensuring CFC meets applicable federal and state requirements as a Sponsor organization. The Coordinator will  support program implementation, day-to-day operations, and continued development of CFC’s newest Medicaid meal delivery program.

The Program Coordinator will manage a variety of daily administrative and program responsibilities, including recordkeeping, partner onboarding and support, site visits, program audits, service expansion, and communications. The Program Coordinator will work closely with partners to ensure they have the information and resources needed to successfully provide services while meeting required program timelines and deadlines.

The Program Coordinator must be able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment and support CFC programs as needs evolve throughout the year. Travel to different regions of Colorado will be required.

This position includes a 30-day introductory period, after which the employee becomes eligible for health insurance benefits.

Essential Duties/Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Support planning and coordination of ongoing programs and activities for CACFP, Home Delivered Meals through Medicaid, and SFSP.
Proactively and independently manage assigned daily tasks, projects, and program deadlines.
Maintain an understanding of rules, regulations, and policies applicable to Federal Nutrition Programs, stay current on updated requirements, and interpret operational impacts.
Design systems and structures for effective program implementation and expansion efforts for CACFP, Medicaid, and SFSP.
Support monthly CACFP and SFSP claim preparation, including review and reconciliation of attendance, meal counts, enrollment records, Income Eligibility Forms, menus, production records, and other required documentation.
Identify missing, incomplete, expired, or noncompliant documentation and communicate necessary corrections to participating sites prior to claim submission.
Track claim deadlines and required program submissions to ensure timely and accurate reporting.
Support preparation and organization of program records for state reviews, audits, and other oversight activities.
Conduct required federal onsite monitoring visits to providers and caretakers across Colorado, including but not limited to home care providers, afterschool programs, and childcare centers.
Document monitoring findings and communicate required follow-up or corrective actions to participating sites when applicable.
Coordinate with food vendors regarding menus, meal orders, delivery schedules, substitutions, documentation, service issues, and program compliance.
Train and onboard new centers, home providers, vendors, and other partners on CFC processes, documentation requirements, program systems, meal service procedures, and applicable program requirements.
Maintain consistent follow-up with partners regarding outstanding documentation, deadlines, compliance issues, and operational changes.
Engage partners to inform them of program offerings and enroll students, centers, and home providers in meal delivery programs.
Work with community organizations to inform them about programming and support enrollment efforts.
Identify and manage partners with aligned missions and priorities.
Manage daily email and phone communications in the CRM system from families accessing programming.
Support families with program registration platforms and troubleshoot issues.
Develop and disseminate high-quality communications to support program implementation and expansion.
Facilitate external presentations about CFC programs for multiple audiences.
Support development and distribution of external communications, including but not limited to newsletters, social media, and customer service communications.
Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications and Experiences: 

Bachelor's degree or relevant years of experience. 
Registered Dietitian or Certified Nutritionist credential required to support Medicaid program requirements.
2+ of experience working with communities. 
Excellent organizational and time management skills.
Detail-oriented and efficient.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong attention to detail and demonstrated ability to review documentation for accuracy and completeness.
Ability to communicate expectations, deadlines, and compliance concerns professionally with external partners.
Ability to execute projects from development phase to operation.
Experience implementing public programming preferably programs funded through federal funds.
Ability to work independently in a remote work environment while maintaining consistent communication, documentation, and accountability.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines while maintaining accurate and organized records.
Have access to reliable transportation.
Have a valid drivers license.
Ability to travel to all areas of Colorado as needed.

Preferred Qualifications and Experience:

Candidates who are bilingual are strongly encouraged to apply.
Focus and special interest in food insecurity, childcare and policy.
Experience with CACFP, SFSP, Medicaid, or other federal/state nutrition or human services programs. 
Proficiency working in Google Suite.
Problem Solver.
Strong understanding of community engagement strategies.

About The Role

We have exciting opportunities for Newly Qualified Social Workers, Social Workers and Senior Social Workers to join our Transitions Service.

Whether you are starting your social work career or looking to build on your existing experience, you will play a vital role in supporting people to live meaningful lives, achieve their goals and have a voice in decisions about their care and support.

For Newly Qualified Social Workers, we offer a structured and supportive Assessed and Supported Year in Employment (ASYE) programme, delivered alongside experienced Advanced Practice Leads and Learning and Development colleagues. This provides a strong foundation for developing confidence, skills and professional practice.

As a Social Worker, you will manage a varied and rewarding caseload, working with individuals, families, carers and partner agencies to assess needs, manage risk, develop strengths-based support plans and promote positive outcomes. You will undertake a range of statutory duties, including safeguarding enquiries, Mental Capacity Act assessments, care and support planning, and reviews.

As a Senior Social Worker, alongside managing complex work, you will provide practice leadership and support the development of others through mentoring, coaching, practice education and assessment. You will play an important role in promoting high-quality practice and supporting continuous learning within the team.

Our social workers are part of a strong multi-agency network across Leeds, working closely with health colleagues, providers and community organisations to deliver person-centred support. We value professional curiosity, reflective practice and collaborative working, recognising that the best outcomes are achieved when people, families and professionals work together.

You will be supported by experienced Team Managers, Senior Social Workers, Advanced Practitioners and Safeguarding and Risk Managers who are committed to creating a positive learning culture. We strive to provide the right balance of support and challenge, with clear opportunities for development and progression throughout your career.

Above all, this is an opportunity to make a genuine difference to the lives of adults with learning disabilities while developing your own skills, knowledge and professional journey within a supportive and ambitious service.

Our Better Lives Strategy sets out our ambition for improving lives in Leeds. We want people with care and support needs to be able to do the things that matter to them and live in a good home within a caring community. It’s about more than social care, it’s a council-wide initiative so that services will work together to make a real difference to individuals and their communities.

Degree or equivalent in Social Work
Registered with Social Work England
Have an interest in working with young people transitioning from Children’s services to Adult’s services.
An enthusiasm to work as part of a multidisciplinary team.

Knowledge and understanding of current social work practice (children’s and/or adults) and the role of multidisciplinary working, including statutory, voluntary and community organisations.
Skills in assessment, care planning, intervention and evaluation to support young people to achieve positive outcomes.
Experience of adopting a person-centred approach, using creativity in problem solving and applying reflective practice to support professional development.
A commitment to learning and development, including successful completion of the Assessed and Supported Year in Employment (ASYE) programme.

A minimum of two years' post-qualifying social work experience.
The ability to build and maintain effective working relationships with colleagues, partner agencies, individuals, families and carers.
Experience of chairing meetings, coordinating multi-agency working and representing the Council in a range of professional settings.

In addition to the above, Senior Social Workers will bring:

The ability to lead, motivate, mentor and supervise others to deliver high-quality social work practice.
A commitment to the ongoing professional development of both themselves and others.
The confidence to provide practice leadership, support decision-making and promote continuous improvement across the service.

What We Offer You

We take pride in offering the best employee experience, with benefits including:

a competitive salary and annual leave entitlement plus statutory holidays
membership of the West Yorkshire Pension Fund with generous employer contributions
flexible and hybrid working arrangements subject to service requirements
a clear career pathway and continuing professional development opportunities
a range of staff benefits to help you boost your wellbeing and make your money go further

Please complete the online application form.

Read our guidance for further advice. Please check your information carefully and ensure you complete all sections before submitting your application.

If you have any queries or would like an informal chat about the role please contact:

Lynn Dunion, or Sian Bishop ( Transitions Team Managers) on 0113 3784700 or sian.bishop@leeds.gov.uk , Lynn.dunion@leeds.gov.uk

A Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check will be carried out on preferred candidates. Read our recruitment of ex-offenders policy .

We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults.

We promote diversity and want a workforce that reflects the population of Leeds. We are also an Age friendly employer, a Mindful employer and a Disability Confident leader .

All new Leeds City Council appointments are made subject to the satisfactory completion of a six-month probationary period.

This role is based in the UK. Home Office guidance states that candidates must evidence their right to work in the UK prior to commencing employment, either as a UK or Irish citizen, under the EU Settlement scheme or having secured any other relevant work visa.  

If you do not have the right to work in the UK, you must consider your own eligibility for sponsorship for a particular role through the  Skilled Worker visa route before applying. To be eligible for sponsorship you'll usually need to be paid the standard salary rate of at least £41,700 per year or meet one of the other eligibility criteria. Ensure you are eligible before applying.

Special conditions
this post is subject to a higher level check with the Disclosure and Barring Service. Please note that a criminal record will not necessarily be a bar to obtaining employment; this will depend on the circumstances and background to any offence.

With the support and guidance of the Team Manager, you will provide a high-quality, strengths-based social work service to young people, their families and carers. Working within statutory frameworks, organisational policies and professional standards, you will assess needs, manage risk, promote wellbeing and support individuals to achieve positive outcomes and greater independence.

You will work collaboratively with colleagues, partner agencies and local communities to deliver person-centred support, ensuring practice is informed by relevant legislation, policy and best practice. Manage a varied and often complex caseload of adults with learning disabilities, undertaking assessments, support planning, reviews and risk management in accordance with relevant legislation, policy and procedures.
Work collaboratively with young people, families, carers and partner agencies to identify strengths, needs and desired outcomes, promoting choice, independence and wellbeing.
Undertake person-centred Care Act assessments and develop, implement and review care and support plans that reflect assessed needs and available resources.
Safeguard young adults at risk by undertaking enquiries, assessing and managing risk, and working within local and national safeguarding procedures.
Work alongside Children’s Services to safeguarding children under 18.
Build and maintain effective working relationships with colleagues and professionals across health, Children’s social care, Adult’s Social Care, housing, education, advocacy and voluntary sector organisations to deliver coordinated support.
Provide direct intervention, advice and support to young people, families and carers, helping them to make informed decisions and access appropriate services and community resources.
Analyse complex information, exercise professional judgement and make evidence-based decisions in relation to care planning, risk management and safeguarding.
Maintain accurate, timely and professional records, assessments and reports in accordance with legislative, organisational and professional requirements.
Prepare clear and accurate reports, assessments and case records, contributing to legal and formal processes where appropriate, with support from experienced colleagues.
Prepare and deliver presentations, briefings and information sessions to internal teams, partner organisations, young people and families, communicating complex information clearly, confidently and accurately
Have knowledge and experience in applying the Mental Capacity Act 2005 and best interests decision-making, undertaking assessments appropriate to your level of experience with support, guidance and supervision from experienced colleagues.
Commission, monitor and review services and support arrangements, ensuring they deliver positive outcomes and represent value for money.
Participate in the screening of referrals and respond to urgent situations through duty arrangements, assessing risk and implementing appropriate interventions.
Contribute to service improvement by identifying opportunities to develop practice, improve processes and promote innovative approaches to supporting people.
Work in accordance with relevant legislation, professional standards, policies, procedures and the Social Work England professional standards.
Make effective use of supervision, continuous professional development and reflective practice to maintain and enhance professional competence.
Promote equality, diversity and inclusion, ensuring anti-discriminatory and strengths-based practice in all aspects of work.

In addition to the responsibilities of an ASYE Social Worker, experienced Social Workers will:

Following a minimum of two years' post-qualifying experience and with appropriate support and supervision, undertake Mental Capacity Act and Best Interests Assessments in accordance with relevant legislation, completing assessments and associated documentation within statutory timescales and making recommendations regarding authorisations and representation where required.
Lead and contribute to complex assessments, care planning, risk management and decision-making in relation to adults with learning disabilities, their families and carers.
Manage a complex and varied caseload, exercising professional judgement and autonomy within legislative, policy and procedural frameworks.

As a Senior Social Worker, alongside managing complex work, you will provide practice leadership and support the development of others through mentoring, coaching, practice education and assessment. You will play an important role in promoting high-quality practice and supporting continuous learning within the team.

Our social workers are part of a strong multi-agency network across Leeds, working closely with health colleagues, providers and community organisations to deliver person-centred support. We value professional curiosity, reflective practice and collaborative working, recognising that the best outcomes are achieved when people, families and professionals work together.

You will be supported by experienced Team Managers, Senior Social Workers, Advanced Practitioners and Safeguarding and Risk Managers who are committed to creating a positive learning culture. We strive to provide the right balance of support and challenge, with clear opportunities for development and progression throughout your career.

Above all, this is an opportunity to make a genuine difference to the lives of adults with learning disabilities while developing your own skills, knowledge and professional journey within a supportive and ambitious service.

Our Better Lives Strategy sets out our ambition for improving lives in Leeds. We want people with care and support needs to be able to do the things that matter to them and live in a good home within a caring community. It’s about more than social care, it’s a council-wide initiative so that services will work together to make a real difference to individuals and their communities.

Job Description

Special conditions
this post is subject to a higher level check with the Disclosure and Barring Service. Please note that a criminal record will not necessarily be a bar to obtaining employment; this will depend on the circumstances and background to any offence.

Job Purpose

With the support and guidance of the Team Manager, you will provide a high-quality, strengths-based social work service to young people, their families and carers. Working within statutory frameworks, organisational policies and professional standards, you will assess needs, manage risk, promote wellbeing and support individuals to achieve positive outcomes and greater independence.

You will work collaboratively with colleagues, partner agencies and local communities to deliver person-centred support, ensuring practice is informed by relevant legislation, policy and best practice. At all times, you will carry out your responsibilities in accordance with Leeds City Council's values, policies and procedures, and the professional standards set by Social Work England

Responsibilities

The duties outlined below are not exhaustive and may be amended to meet the changing needs of the service, provided they remain consistent with the grade and purpose of the post.

Manage a varied and often complex caseload of adults with learning disabilities, undertaking assessments, support planning, reviews and risk management in accordance with relevant legislation, policy and procedures.
Work collaboratively with young people, families, carers and partner agencies to identify strengths, needs and desired outcomes, promoting choice, independence and wellbeing.
Undertake person-centred Care Act assessments and develop, implement and review care and support plans that reflect assessed needs and available resources.
Safeguard young adults at risk by undertaking enquiries, assessing and managing risk, and working within local and national safeguarding procedures.
Work alongside Children’s Services to safeguarding children under 18.
Build and maintain effective working relationships with colleagues and professionals across health, Children’s social care, Adult’s Social Care, housing, education, advocacy and voluntary sector organisations to deliver coordinated support.
Provide direct intervention, advice and support to young people, families and carers, helping them to make informed decisions and access appropriate services and community resources.
Analyse complex information, exercise professional judgement and make evidence-based decisions in relation to care planning, risk management and safeguarding.
Maintain accurate, timely and professional records, assessments and reports in accordance with legislative, organisational and professional requirements.
Prepare clear and accurate reports, assessments and case records, contributing to legal and formal processes where appropriate, with support from experienced colleagues.
Prepare and deliver presentations, briefings and information sessions to internal teams, partner organisations, young people and families, communicating complex information clearly, confidently and accurately
Have knowledge and experience in applying the Mental Capacity Act 2005 and best interests decision-making, undertaking assessments appropriate to your level of experience with support, guidance and supervision from experienced colleagues.
Commission, monitor and review services and support arrangements, ensuring they deliver positive outcomes and represent value for money.
Participate in the screening of referrals and respond to urgent situations through duty arrangements, assessing risk and implementing appropriate interventions.
Contribute to service improvement by identifying opportunities to develop practice, improve processes and promote innovative approaches to supporting people.
Work in accordance with relevant legislation, professional standards, policies, procedures and the Social Work England professional standards.
Make effective use of supervision, continuous professional development and reflective practice to maintain and enhance professional competence.
Promote equality, diversity and inclusion, ensuring anti-discriminatory and strengths-based practice in all aspects of work.

Specific Responsibilities For Experienced Social Workers

In addition to the responsibilities of an ASYE Social Worker, experienced Social Workers will:

Following a minimum of two years' post-qualifying experience and with appropriate support and supervision, undertake Mental Capacity Act and Best Interests Assessments in accordance with relevant legislation, completing assessments and associated documentation within statutory timescales and making recommendations regarding authorisations and representation where required.
Lead and contribute to complex assessments, care planning, risk management and decision-making in relation to adults with learning disabilities, their families and carers.
Manage a complex and varied caseload, exercising professional judgement and autonomy within legislative, policy and procedural frameworks.
